title: cksum-based pane-liveness check is defeated by the CLI's own continuously-incrementing elapsed-time/token-count text, so a genuinely hung fixer is never recognized as frozen past the 180-minute ceiling
description: self-fix.sh:33-45 (round-6 patch for FIND-027) tries to distinguish 'real progress' from 'hung' once a fixer session is older than MAX_FIXER_MIN=180: it captures the pane, cksums the last 25 lines, and compares against the previous capture stored in PANEHASH. If the pane shows 'esc to interrupt' in its last 6 lines AND the cksum differs from last time, it concludes 'real progress, continue' (self-fix.sh:41-42); only if the cksum is UNCHANGED does it conclude 'hung' and kill+respawn (self-fix.sh:44-45). This is unsound: the Claude Code CLI's own status/spinner line embeds a continuously-incrementing elapsed-time and/or token counter that updates on every render tick, independent of whether the underlying awaited tool call (e.g. a hung network request or a browser waitForSelector with no timeout) is making any real progress. The builder's OWN test fixtures in test-healthcheck-lib.sh document exactly this format: line 16 '✻ Brewed for 3m · esc to interrupt' and line 29 '✢ Searching… (7m · ↓ 19k tokens · esc to interrupt)' -- both contain a live elapsed-time/token count that differs from one capture to the next purely due to time passing, with zero relation to real task progress. Because this text sits inside the very same last-25-lines block that is cksum'd (self-fix.sh:39), ANY two pane captures taken more than a few seconds apart while the CLI is alive and rendering will produce different cksums -- even when the actual tool call is completely deadlocked. self-fix.sh:34's own comment claims the opposite premise ('a hung curl/waitForSelector shows the same spinner forever'), which is contradicted by the very fixture text the builder wrote elsewhere in this codebase. Net effect: the code path that is supposed to detect and kill a genuinely stuck fixer (the entire point of FIND-023/FIND-027) will, for the realistic hang mode this fixer is explicitly built to hit (browser/network automation per self-fix.sh's own TASK text at lines 51-58), almost always take the 'still progressing' branch and never fire the kill+respawn branch -- because the CLI's elapsed-time counter alone guarantees cur != prev on every check.
concreteFailureScenario: A dispatched Opus fixer opens CloakBrowser and calls waitForSelector on an element that will never appear (site changed, selector stale) with no timeout, or issues a curl to a dead endpoint with no --max-time. The Claude Code CLI process itself stays alive and keeps redrawing its status line with an incrementing 'Xm Ys · esc to interrupt' (or token count) every render tick even though the awaited call never returns. Every subsequent self-fix.sh invocation past the 180-min ceiling -- whether triggered every ~5min by cascading healthcheck escalation (healthcheck-lib.sh's _restart() re-calls _selffix on every run once the 5-restarts/60min threshold is crossed, without writing a new RESTART_LOG entry, so escalation repeats each cycle) or every 6h by verify-loops-audit.sh -- captures a pane whose cksum differs from the prior capture purely because of the timer/token text, so self-fix.sh:41-42 fires 'real progress, continue' forever. The underlying loop (capafy/reddit/life-manager) remains DEAD/broken indefinitely, self-heal never recovers it, and no human is watching. This is a de-facto permanent-disable of the self-heal path for this class of hang -- the exact invariant round 6 was asked to confirm is NOT broken.

evidence.snippet:
PANEHASH="$STATE/.self-fix-$LOOP.panehash"
_pane="$(tmux -S "$SOCK" capture-pane -t "$SESSION" -p 2>/dev/null)"
cur="$(printf '%s' "$_pane" | tail -25 | cksum | awk '{print $1"-"$2}')"
prev="$(cat "$PANEHASH" 2>/dev/null||echo none)"; printf '%s' "$cur" > "$PANEHASH"
if printf '%s' "$_pane" | tail -6 | grep -qE 'esc to interrupt' && [ "$cur" != "$prev" ]; then
  ... 'real progress, continue' ...
fi
... 'hung → kill+respawn' ...

supportingEvidence.snippet: '✻ Brewed for 3m · esc to interrupt' ... '✢ Searching… (7m · ↓ 19k tokens · esc to interrupt)'
